title: Bridging the Last Mile of Circuit Design: PostEDA-Bench, a Hierarchical Benchmark for PPA Convergence and DRC Fixing
abstract: arXiv:2605.06936v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly applied to the "last mile" of Electronic Design Automation (EDA): repairing residual sign-off Design Rule Check (DRC) violations and converging Power-Performance-Area (PPA) targets after tool runs. Existing EDA-LLM benchmarks, however, omit DRC fixing entirely and rely on flat hierarchies tied to a single toolchain. We introduce PostEDA-Bench, a hierarchical benchmark with 145 tasks across DRC-Essential, DRC-Reasoning, PPA-Mono, and PPA-Multi, supported by EDA toolchains with machine-checkable evaluation. Across eight commercial and open-source LLMs under multiple agent scaffolds, we find that agents handle synthetic DRC-Essential and single-objective PPA-Mono reasonably well but degrade sharply on the more practical DRC-Reasoning, where the best success rate is 36.66%, and PPA-Multi, where the best success rate is 20.00%; vision augmentation consistently enhances DRC-Bench; and trade-off reaso

translated_title: 打通电路设计的最后一英里：PostEDA-Bench，一个面向PPA收敛与DRC修复的分层基准测试
translated_abstract: 基于大语言模型（LLM）的智能体正被越来越多地应用于电子设计自动化（EDA）的“最后一英里”：即在工具运行后修复残留的签字确认设计规则检查违规，并收敛功耗-性能-面积（PPA）目标。然而，现有的EDA-LLM基准测试完全忽略了DRC修复，且依赖与单一工具链绑定的扁平层级结构。我们提出了PostEDA-Bench，这是一个包含145个任务的分层基准测试，涵盖DRC-Essential、DRC-Reasoning、PPA-Mono和PPA-Multi四个类别，并由具备机器可检验评估的EDA工具链提供支持。在多种智能体框架下对八个商业和开源LLM进行评估后，我们发现智能体在合成性的DRC-Essential和单目标PPA-Mono任务上表现尚可，但在更贴近实际场景的DRC-Reasoning任务上性能急剧下降（最佳成功率为36.66%），在PPA-Multi任务上同样如此（最佳成功率为20.00%）；视觉增强持续提升了DRC-Bench的表现；权衡推理……（摘要原文在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了PostEDA-Bench——首个面向EDA“最后一英里”的分层基准测试，包含145个DRC修复与PPA收敛任务并配备机器可检验评估，评估显示当前LLM智能体在实用的DRC推理和多目标PPA优化任务上最佳成功率分别仅为36.66%和20.00%，揭示了现有模型与真实后端设计需求之间的显著差距。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces PostEDA-Bench, a hierarchical benchmark with 145 machine-checkable tasks covering DRC fixing and PPA convergence in the last mile of EDA, revealing that current LLM agents degrade sharply on practical DRC reasoning and multi-objective PPA tasks, with best success rates of only 36.66% and 20.00% respectively.
